newsitem.title: USA: Americans try low-fat foods, but eat more burgers.
newsitem.headline: Americans try low-fat foods, but eat more burgers.

text.p: Americans may be aware of the perils of a fatty diet judging by the numbers who give low-fat foods a try, but they gulped down millions more hamburgers and french fries this year, a new survey has found.

About seven out of eight Americans consumed at least one low-fat or fat-free food in a typical two-week period, yet they collectively wolfed down almost six million more hamburgers, eight million more orders of fries and five million more helpings of chicken nuggets than they did in a similar two-week period a year ago.

The survey of 2,000 households that kept dietary diaries and mailed them in each day was released this week by NBD Group, a marketing research company specialising in food trends in the Chicago suburb of Rosemont, Illinois.

"We've seen a decline in the number of people who say they try foods that are healthy," NBD Group's Marilyn Parille said. "Because more of us are overweight, less of us are concerned with (dietary) fat."

Americans' concern about cholesterol, salt, additives, preservatives, caffeine and sugar in their diets peaked in 1990, the survey, in its 11th year, showed. In 1990, 51 percent said they were concerned with cholesterol, while this year only 38 percent paid attention.
Meanwhile many felt they were doing themselves a favour by gorging on low-fat cookies, cakes and ice cream.

"We call it the 'Snackwell syndrome', where people think they can eat a whole box of cookies and not gain weight," nutrition expert Bonnie Liebman of the Centre for Science in the Public Interest said of the popular brand of low-fat cookie.
"A lot of people haven't got the message or don't believe it," Liebman said of the pleas to eat more fruits, vegetables, grains and beans. "And they're not sure how to eat less fat."
Many of those additional fat-filled takeout meals were consumed in cars, although the average family shared five dinners a week at home, the NBD survey found.
